title: Traffic-aware canary orchestrator with Terraform preflight + runtime hooks
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Create an orchestrator that ties Terraform preflight validation and runtime traffic-weighted canary promotions for private (VPC) control plane upgrades. The goal is a repeatable, auditable pipeline that runs IaC checks, warms runtime caches, and promotes new control plane versions by slicing tenant traffic based on live telemetry and automated health gates.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform preflight step runs automatically and fails fast with actionable diagnostics when infra drift or plan changes would block an upgrade
Canary promotion is driven by real-time telemetry: error rate, p50/p95 latency, and tenant-specific health signals
Ability to define per-tenant traffic weights and automatic ramping policies (e.g., 1%, 5%, 25%, 100%)
Rollback triggers defined and exercised in chaos/smoke tests; rollback completes within configured window and leaves clusters stable
All orchestration steps are auditable in Console with links to plan logs, PRs, and the upgrade runbook
design_decision_log: Decision: Use Terraform Cloud/Enterprise run API for immutable preflight - triggers run, captures plan artifacts and outputs. Trade-off: depends on network connectivity from control plane; mitigated via short-lived bastion and signed artifacts.

Decision: Traffic slicing implemented at the routing layer in control-plane proxy rather than DNS to achieve per-tenant granularity and sub-second pivots. Trade-off: added complexity in routing rules; preferred for faster rollback.

Decision: Cache-warming step added post-canary promotion to reduce first-token latency for promoted version. Chosen approach: synthetic prefix replay (small sample of tenant prefixes). Trade-off: extra load during promotion window; limited to low-QPS synthetic traffic.
Decision: Gate thresholds set by SRE + PM: p95 latency increase <= 15% and error rate delta <= 0.5% absolute for canary to advance. These will be adjustable via feature flags during initial rollouts.
implementation_plan: 1) IaC: add terraform module hooks that create a canary_release resource and an api token for preflight runs
2) Preflight: wire a Lambda/runner to kick Terraform run and persist plan.json to GCS/S3 for audit
3) Orchestrator: implement traffic weight controller in control plane service with API endpoints for phased promotions
4) Telemetry: add canary-specific metrics (canary_error_rate, canary_latency_percentiles) and a short retention time stream for rapid decisions
5) UI: Console page to visualize canary progress, show plan artifacts, and provide manual override
6) Automation: create a promotion policy engine that applies gating rules and advances weights on success or triggers rollback on failure
7) Integrations: link GitHub PRs and changelogs into the run summary and emit audit log entries into the existing audit pipeline
tests_and_telemetry: Create synthetic workload generator that replays representative request prefixes for 10 tenants during canary windows
Smoke tests: deploy canary in staging and run chaos scenarios (latency injection, partial KV cache loss) to validate gating and rollback
Dashboard: new per-release dashboard in Console with canary timeline, weight history, and gating metrics
Alerts: automated Slack + PagerDuty trigger when gating thresholds breach or when promotion fails to progress for > 30m
Postmortem collection: each failed promotion auto-opens an incident card template linking the plan artifact and the rollout trace
